# the contributor audit: cap rotations, selected-star escape, unequal triangles

## Normal motion and global cancellation: PASS

I read `candidate cd3cb3fa09220cc8`
in full and ran the verifier: 29 groups and 441 exact decreasing cap
paths pass, along with positive dependence and section cancellation.

Fixing the entire affine meeting section is the correct coverage
condition. The positive-spanning bound is uniform over all directions
and all ambient points, including the section itself. The counterexample
to preserving only a common point is correct. The statement also retains
the compatibility of a cap shared by several groups; independently
moving duplicate labeled occurrences is not automatically an allowed
motion of a single shared constraint.

The coarea coefficient is the reciprocal continuous-normal length.
For a proper convex-fiber section, its relative interior is inside the
fiber's interior and its relative boundary is null; bounded supports
then justify the swept-length dominated-convergence derivative.
Strict full/empty traces persist. Supporting traces are explicitly
outside this differentiability assertion. In dimension one the proper
section uses counting measure, with the separate stated exception.

The barycentric residual identities and the two definitions of the
physical normal motion agree with their stated (different) metrics.
The combined meeting-point and normal motion makes each cap derivative
exactly `-S_i`. The inverse-transpose Neumann estimate proves a positive
dependence for the actual moved margins, and hence exact full-space
coverage. Canonical groups cannot all improve, by the ordinary centroid
bound. The star's two endpoint section moments cancel, and the middle
moment vanishes by symmetry. A single inclusion-minimal circuit already
has this cancellation, without inheriting the multigroup variance stress.

## Selected critical star escape: PASS

I read `candidate 9b703b460ed5bf2b`
in full and ran its standard-library verifier. All 22 exact identities
and paths and 168 isolated planar cap-budget checks pass.

The central identity is valid even while the thresholds move:
`mu_W(H_i(a))=D+F_i(W,a)-F_i(I,a)`. The subtracted term is the
changing reflected-endpoint contribution, not a discarded constant.
The column l1 bound proves strict actual midpoint compatibility.
The determinant and proper-cut sign conditions make all rational
formulas analytic in a genuine neighborhood of the reference body.

At nonuniform thresholds the explicit derivative right inverse supplies
the strictly improving physical velocity. At canonical thresholds,
`a(t)=1/m+t(e_1-e_0)` has `J=(d-1)t/d`; the fixed elementary matrix
choice makes its velocity analytic through zero. Composing the endpoint
motion with `t^2` gives positive volume and negative cap coefficients
of order `t^3`, with uniformly bounded remainders of order `t^4`.
Consequently every joint neighborhood contains an actual improvement.

In the binary extension, compactness of the finite fixed fibers allows
uniformly strict finite isolation tilts for all nearby thresholds.
Regular cap masses remain exactly `D`; star caps decrease. Coverage,
integer support and center membership are all retained. An unchanged
regular centroid and the retained cover prove maximum absolute depth
exactly `D` while the total mass increases. Only selected cap budgets
are preserved; the redundant discarded constraints are not claimed
feasible. This limitation is explicit and essential.

## Unequal homothetic triangles: PASS

I read `candidate 61737978508b9a80`
in full and ran the correctly named standard-library verifier
`supporting computation verify_unequal_triangle_pair_below_ordinary_sum.py`. All 135 family
certificates and 576 ordinary-cap checks pass.

The ordinary depths use the already proved all-normal `4BC` formula,
and the displayed common-normal caps have exactly the asserted areas.
The broad family's shortfall is `(s-r)(r+s-2L)V>0`; its specified
epsilon keeps both cuts proper and retains at least half the gap.
The limiting ratio of the upper certificate to the sum of ordinary
depths is `3/4`. No lower bound with that factor and no assertion of
paired optimality are made. This remains an auxiliary counterexample,
not an OC counterexample or a statement about all actual middle fibers.

## Quadratic escape and flat compatibility normalization: PASS

I read `candidate 30d7d56bee7b8657`, including
its general symmetric-source extension, and ran its verifier: all 36
exact checks pass. The pure threshold Hessian vanishes only after the
unchanged-source cap contribution is included. The mixed block appears
twice in the joint quadratic form, giving the asserted positive `Q`.
The right inverse pays each cap separately, and the common analytic
proper-cut neighborhood controls every remainder. The general extension
uses an allowed continuous shear and the corrected negative base sign;
only the entire original source's cap sum is constant as parameters
move. Its explicit free-simplex feasibility assumption is retained.

I also read `candidate 2c18dd3b9615c3c4`
in full and ran its verifier: all 64 exact excluded-target relations
and six actual physical paths pass. The normalization preserves total
volume and EACH selected shared canonical cap mass exactly. Removing
the target's self-weight gives the nonvanishing uniform Jensen gap;
the Hausdorff support bounds prove an open neighborhood of genuine
independent convex-fiber changes. Lattice completeness excludes extra
integer fibers, while positive inballs and full base rank ensure a
full-dimensional ambient hull.

The unequal-volume scaling of the two positive modes cancels every
first cap derivative exactly. The volume-unit right inverse and its
chosen acceleration then give strictly signed second derivatives.
Because the preliminary strictification is flat in both objective
and budgets, no first-order budget loss overwhelms this later gain.
The affine shear, saturated-lattice relative version and d=1 obstruction
are all correctly stated. The relative deficient-base version does not
claim an unproved full-ambient completion. This is a selected-cover
variation theorem for a class already known to be OC-safe, not an
arbitrary-cover classification.

## Monotone four-triangle theorem: PASS

I read `candidate 680d45e380747dc3` in full
and ran the verifier. The exact envelope follows from the derivative
sign of the one-vertex cut formula, including its coordinate and
repeated-height limits. Both scalar inequalities hold on their entire
real parameter intervals; the proof does not use the numerical profile
screens. In particular radius growth is at least two thirds of the
squared-radius growth in its stated range.

The heavy alternative and all three tilt ranges exhaust every real
tilt. The use of the earlier positive-normal reduction is at an actual
own centroid, with compatible common-vertex fibers, so its hypotheses
hold. Its finite replacement covers vertical caps with boundary mass.
The later envelope relaxation may select different positive normals
fiber by fiber, but it is used in the correct lower-bound direction
and retains one tilt. The three scalar bounds meet without gaps.
The proof establishes exactly its monotone four-fiber scope; an interior
peak and arbitrary counts remain separate questions. All 169 scalar,
4212 envelope and 343 growth checks pass, including exact all-tilt
minimization on the tested nonheavy profiles.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
